wu: Count and Catch: Students stand in a circle and throw a soft pumpkin. They count from 1 to 10 in order, each student saying one number. If a student drops the pumpkin or says the wrong number, they sit down. The last student standing wins.
wuAlt: Number Bingo: Teacher calls out numbers 1-10 in English, students cover the corresponding number on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Halloween Count: Teacher shows flashcards of Halloween items (e.g., 3 bats, 5 ghosts), students shout the number in English.
pres: Teacher uses a big storybook about a pumpkin patch. Pointing to pumpkins, models 'This is my pumpkin. It is big/scary!' and 'How many pumpkins?' Students repeat chorally. Teacher writes numbers 1-10 on the board and says 'plus, minus, equals' with simple sums (e.g., 2 + 1 = 3). Students hold up fingers to show answers.
presAlt: Number Hopscotch: Draw a hopscotch grid with numbers 1-10. Students jump and say the number they land on. Teacher calls out 'Jump to 5!' or 'Jump to 8!'.
Pumpkin Craft Demo: Teacher shows a paper pumpkin craft, saying 'I need 1 orange paper. I need 2 eyes. I need 1 mouth.' Students repeat the sentences.
prac: Pair Race: Students work in pairs. Each pair gets a set of number cards 1-10. Teacher calls out a sum (e.g., '3 plus 2!'). The first pair to find the answer card (5) and hold it up wins a point. Teacher models 'Three plus two equals five!'
pracAlt: Pumpkin Counting Game: Students get a bowl of plastic spiders. Teacher says 'Put 4 spiders on your pumpkin!' Students do it and say 'Four spiders!'.
Number Chain Story: Students sit in a circle. Each student adds one sentence to a story using a number, e.g., 'I see 1 bat. I see 2 cats...'. Teacher starts the story.
ls: Listen and Draw: Teacher reads a short Halloween story with numbers, e.g., 'There are 3 pumpkins. 2 pumpkins are big. 1 pumpkin is small.' Students draw the pumpkins as they listen. Teacher checks drawings for correct numbers and sizes.
re: Zombie Tag: One student is 'it' (zombie) and chases others. When tagged, students freeze and say a number 1-10. Another student can 'unfreeze' them by saying the next number. Game continues until all are frozen.
prod: Pumpkin Costume Project: Students design their own Halloween costume on paper. They label parts in English, e.g., 'This is my mask. It is scary. I have a cape.' They present their costume to the class, saying 'This is my costume. It is [adjective]. I have [item].'
rw: Number Problem Writing: Students write 2 simple maths problems for a partner, e.g., '5 plus 3 equals?' and '10 minus 4 equals?'. They swap papers and solve the problems, writing the answers numerals.
st: Teacher reads a short Halloween counting story, e.g., 'Ten Little Pumpkins'. Students count along with the story. End with the 'Goodbye Song' and a sticker chart. Students line up for high-fives as they leave.
g: Teacher calls out numbers 1-10. Students cover the number on their bingo card. First to shout 'Bingo!' wins.
Students take turns rolling a dice and putting that many plastic spiders on their paper pumpkin. First to 10 spiders wins.
Teacher writes a sum on the board. Students race to write the answer on their mini-whiteboard. First correct wins.
Teacher shows a flashcard of a costume (e.g., 'witch'). Students say 'This is a witch. It is scary.'
Students throw a ball and count how many times they catch it without dropping it.
diff: Fast finishers: Write 3 more maths problems for a friend.
Support learners: Use number lines or fingers to solve sums.
hw: Interview a family member: 'What is your favourite number? Why?' Write 2 answers.
Draw your dream Halloween costume and label 3 parts in English.
Count 10 things in your house and write them in a list, e.g., '1 table, 2 chairs...'.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references, like comparing Halloween to local festivals, to make the theme relatable. For example, 'Halloween is like a fun party where we dress up, just like during the Green March!'
